info.title: OpenGame API
info.summary: Deploy games from a terminal, and give a running game identity and leaderboards.
info.description:
Two origins share this document.

- **https://opengame.io/api/v1** is the creator API. The CLI, CI and your own tools call it with a creator token (`ogt_`). An older `oga_` jam upload token is refused. The creator API never runs inside a game.
- **https://api.opengame.gg/v1** is the game API. A running game calls it with the session token the OpenGame page handed it.

Before launch, every creator route except `GET /api/v1/status` and sign-in answers 403 `not_launched` to an account outside the OpenGame team. `GET /api/v1/status` returns whether OpenGame is launched and whether your account may use it.

An account without access to the creator API gets 403 `not_member`, and a suspended or deleted account gets 403 `account_inactive`. Analytics, audience and embed routes add their own rules, listed on each operation.

Creator analytics take no filters. Any filter parameter is refused with `filters_removed`; use the breakdown rows in the weekly report instead.

creatorToken.description: An `ogt_` token from `opengame login` or a browser-minted CI token. An older `oga_` jam upload token is refused as `token_invalid`. Pass it in `Authorization: Bearer`. A token from `opengame login` is refused as `token_invalid` once it goes 90 days without a request, so run `opengame login` again. A token made in settings does not lapse. Revoke either kind in settings.

browserSession.name: sb-<project>-auth-token
browserSession.description: Browser only. A signed-in opengame.io browser session, in the site's session cookie, `sb-<project>-auth-token`, split into `.0`, `.1` and so on when it is long. Only the signed-in private game page calls these operations; a token or a generated client cannot. The examples send it as `$OPENGAME_BROWSER_COOKIE`, which you set to the whole `name=value` pair. A change also needs the header `Origin: https://opengame.io`, which a browser sends and the examples include; without it the answer is 403 `forbidden`.

gameSession.description: The session token the OpenGame page hands a game. It names the game, host and player, so nothing in a request body can.

error.description: A stable code. Branch on this, not on `message`.

message.description: One sentence for a person, saying what happened and what to do. A few refusals carry none: the device polling codes, logout's `unauthorized`, and `not_found` from the device and logout routes.

retry.description: Follow the response's retry policy before repeating work.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Wait this many seconds before a later retry. Also sent as `Retry-After`.

requestId.description: Sent with `internal_error` and with an unexpected `temporarily_unavailable`, and as `x-request-id`. Quote it when you report the failure.

url.description: Where the fix happens, when it is a page, for example the claim page with `handle_required`.

token.description: The token a refusal is about, by its public ID and name, never its secret. Sent with `token_revoked`.

problems.description: With `invalid_jam_answers` only: each answer the form refused, with its own message.

reason.description: Why the request was refused. With `token_rejected`: `missing`, `malformed`, `bad-signature`, `expired` or `not-configured`. With `session_rejected`: `identity_changed`. With `rejected`, `unavailable_in_preview` and `preview_unavailable`: a sentence for a person.

refused.description: Events only: events that were malformed.

acceptedIds.description: Events only: always empty on a refusal, so keep every event.

IncrementalDeploy.description: A sorted file manifest and the size, count and hash of its canonical STORE ZIP. Paths must be relative, unique even ignoring case, and cannot name both a file and a folder. Matching hashes must have matching sizes. scoreLabel.description: What the score column is called on the board, such as Round. The board's label is the heading above it.

format.description: How the value reads: number, integer, duration_ms, duration_s, percent (0 to 100) or distance_m.

keep.description: best (the default) keeps each player's best run for each combination of tags. runs keeps every run, up to runsPerPlayer. career keeps one row per player that adds up their accepted runs on the board named by from; nothing is submitted to it.

from.description: Required when keep is career, and refused otherwise: the key of the board of this game whose accepted runs feed this one. It keeps best or runs, not career.

scoreAgg.description: Required when keep is career, and refused otherwise: how a source run's score adds into this board's score. sum, count, max or min.

runsPerPlayer.description: Required when keep is runs, and refused otherwise: how many runs one player keeps on the board for each combination of tags.

format.description: How the value reads: number, integer, duration_ms, duration_s, percent (0 to 100) or distance_m.

decimals.description: How many decimals every value in the column is drawn with, 0 to 4, so a column of rates or averages lines up. A career average or ratio draws one when left out.

agg.description: Career boards only: count, sum, max, min or avg of of over the player's runs, or ratio of two earlier columns.

of.description: Career boards only: score or a column of the source board (a count may leave it out), or for a ratio [numerator, denominator], two earlier columns of this board.

where.description: Career boards only, not on a ratio: count or aggregate only the runs where of compares to value, such as placement eq 1.

scale.description: Ratio only: what the ratio is multiplied by, such as 100 for a percentage. 1 when left out.

requires.description: Ratio only: the ratio is shown only once that earlier column is at least atLeast, such as 5 matches.

each leaderboard column, variant and variant value key is declared once, and no column is keyed score, rank, player, name or all

each column's min is no greater than its max
a career board's from names another board of this game that keeps best or runs, every of and where.of is score or one of that board's columns, and its variants and values are that board's
a career column's ratio divides two columns declared before it that are not ratios, and its requires names one of them; a ratio has no where, and only a ratio has scale or requires
a count may leave of out; every other aggregate names it
room setting keys and choice IDs are unique
each room default names an available choice

AnalyticsSnapshotRequest.description: The window and funnel of a snapshot, named the way the Stats API names them. `from`, `to` and a `timezone` other than UTC are refused as `invalid_range`, never snapped to a nearby week, and the message names `window` and `period`. Any filter, such as `country` or `build`, is refused as `filters_removed`: filters were removed to protect player privacy, and the breakdown rows in the weekly report replace them.

period.description: Which ISO week, such as `2026-W43`. Defaults to the newest complete week. At most 104 weeks back, and never a week starting before 2026-08-01. A week that starts more than 90 days ago has figures only if it was read before then; otherwise they are null and `freshness.unavailable` says why.

filters.description: Accepted only when empty, for clients written before filters were removed. A filter in it is refused as `filters_removed`.

AnalyticsReport.description: The Stats report for one complete ISO week. `window` names it: its `kind` (always `week`), its `period` such as `2026-W43` and its half-open UTC `start` and `end`. `from` and `to` are its Monday and Sunday, `timezone` is always UTC, and `comparison` is the week before. No count describes fewer than 5 players: such a count is null and such a breakdown row is `withheld`. `events` are the game's claims, and an event count is null when its players are withheld. `freshness` says what the figures cover and what is unavailable. A report saved before 22 Oct 2026, read back through a snapshot, export or drain, may lack `window` and carry another timezone. The first report for each week and filter set is kept and served on every later read.

AnalyticsInsights.description: Discovery, source quality, benchmarks and build and session diagnostics. What could not be released is named in `unavailable` rather than shown as zero.

user_code.description: Shown to the person, who types it on the approval page.

post.summary: Take a game off the gallery
post.description: Take a live game off the gallery and stop serving it, as Unpublish does on Your games, through the same function: the game's address answers 410 and tells browsers to drop what they cached, its cover and screenshots come off public storage, and every row and upload is kept. Reversible with `POST /api/v1/games/{id}/restore`. Nothing holds it: a report, a hold or a reviewer does not stop a creator taking their own game down. Requires the `submit` scope on this game; the `deploy` scope makes private previews only, so it cannot take a game down. A banned tester or staff member can still unpublish, as on the website; a banned creator is no longer a member. What `opengame unpublish` sends. No body.

post.description: A batch of named events with allowlisted properties. At most 200 events a request. Each event counts against per-session (600 a minute), per-player (1200) and per-address (3000) budgets; events over budget are counted in `limited` and not stored. String values that look like contact details are dropped. A malformed event is counted in `refused` without failing the rest. Traffic from datacenters and known bots is answered with `filtered: true` and not stored. A private preview's events are accepted and marked, and no rollup counts them. While OpenGame is not taking analytics events, a batch whose events carry `eventId` gets 503 `analytics_unavailable` and should be kept.

eventId.description: Send with `occurredAt`, or leave both out: an event with only one of them is refused. The fourth group must start with 8, 9, `a` or `b`, as `crypto.randomUUID()` writes it. An ID repeated within one batch is refused. Sending the same ID in a later batch is a retry, and the event is stored once.

occurredAt.description: At most 72 hours in the past and 60000 ms in the future.

200.description: Accepted. `acceptedIds` names each event stored; retry the others with the same IDs. Also the answer to a batch with no valid events, and to filtered traffic with `filtered: true`.

get.summary: Read a leaderboard
get.description: `top` needs no session, is cached 30 seconds, and is readable in a browser only from a live game host. `me` returns the player's entry and `around` returns 10 entries either side of it; both need the game's session from that game's host and are not cached. `limit` and `offset` apply to `top` only. `sort` ranks by the score or by a sortable column, each in the order the board sets for it, and `filter` limits the board to runs with those tags. With no filter, the page ranks all the board's runs. On a `keep: "best"` board, each player appears once, by their best run for the sorted column; on a `keep: "runs"` board, each stored run is a row. Only runs with `state` `ok` appear, so a player whose best was clamped gets an empty `me`. From a private preview, every view needs the preview session, `host` may be left out, and only that preview's scores are returned.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The game's host label, for example `derkoloss`. Optional on a private preview.

parameters.name: board
parameters.description: A board key the game declares in `opengame.json`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Never refused: a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more uses the default, and a larger one is clamped.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip before the page, for `top` only. Anything else is refused with `invalid_score_query`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `score`, or the key of a column the board declares sortable. Each sorts in its own declared order.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Tags to narrow the board to, written `key:value` and joined with commas, such as `mode:coop`. Each key and value must be declared by the board.

200.description: Board entries, labeled as the game's claim.

direction.description: The score's order, which the board declares.

preview.description: True on a private preview's board.

total.description: Rows on the board under this filter, counted the way the page ranks them. Null from a game API older than this release, which cannot count them.

sort.description: `score` or the column the page is ranked by.

sortDirection.description: The order of the sorted column.

filter.description: The tags the page is narrowed to. Empty is every run.

post.description: Call it from a live game frame with the session token. Who, which game and which version all come from the token. The body carries the board, the value, and optionally `meta`, the run's `stats` and its `tags`; any other top-level key, and any stat the board does not declare, is dropped and named in `ignored`. A tag the board does not declare is refused. A `keep: "best"` board stores one run per player for each combination of tags; a `keep: "runs"` board stores each run, up to `runsPerPlayer` per player for each combination, and after that replaces that player's lowest-ranked run. Each stat is checked with the column's bounds as the value is with the board's, and the run gets the lower state. A value above the board's `plausible_max` is stored as `plausible_max`, with `state` `clamped` when it is within 10 times the bound and `rejected` beyond that. Values below `plausible_min` are handled the same way. Only scores with `state` `ok` appear on the board. From a private preview, the score goes to that preview's boards and the response includes `preview: true`.

board.description: A board key declared in opengame.json.

stats.description: The run's number for any of the board's columns, keyed by column. Each value is a finite number from -1e15 to 1e15, and 0 or at least 1e-6 from it; at most 512 bytes as JSON.

tags.description: The run's value for any of the board's variants, such as `{"mode":"solo"}`.

200.description: Stored, clamped or refused as implausible.

state.description: `ok` is on the board. `clamped` and `rejected` are kept but not shown.

stored.description: The number kept: the value, or the bound it was clamped to.

best.description: Whether the run was kept on the board: the player's new best on a board that keeps the best, one of their kept runs on a board that keeps runs.

ignored.description: Top-level body keys, then undeclared stats (as `stats.<key>`), that were dropped, each cut to 32 characters. At most 8 body keys are named, with a ninth item reading `…` when there were more, then at most 8 stats.

400.description: `invalid_body`: not a JSON object, or over 2 KB. `rejected`: `reason` names the bad field (`board`, `value`, a `meta` key, a stat that is not a finite number, or a tag the board does not declare).

get.summary: Draw a player's portrait
get.description: The head of an OG as a transparent PNG, as OpenGame shows it next to a name. The address is made only from the look recipe (`og.player.avatar.look`, or `portraitUrl` in `@opengamehq/sdk/avatar`), so it identifies no player and the image at one address stays the same. Every response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`, so a game on another origin can show it or upload it as a WebGL texture.

parameters.name: look
parameters.description: The look recipe: `shape.eyes.color`, then the optional accessory, identity, facial hair and hair colors.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Width and height in pixels. Any other number is redirected to the next listed size up, or to the largest when it is larger. A missing or malformed size is redirected to 256.

parameters.name: theme
parameters.description: `dark` picks the inks OpenGame shows on a dark page, which turns the Auto color (`mono`) white. Any other value, or none, is redirected to `light`.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: The drawing version. An old or missing one is redirected to the current one, 1.

200.description: The portrait, sent as `image/png` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable`. Only an address with all 3 query parameters, in the order `size`, `theme`, `v`, as `portraitUrl` writes it, gets the image.

307.description: Redirects to the canonical address with `size`, `theme` and `v`; follow it. Sent when the request spells the look another way, names an unlisted size, or omits a parameter. A browser and a texture loader follow it on their own; curl needs `--location`.

Location.description: The canonical address, relative to https://opengame.io.

404.description: Not a look OpenGame can draw: an unknown shape, eyes, color or accessory, or a malformed recipe. The response has no body. Show your default character.

429.description: This address asked for too many new portraits in the last hour. The body is JSON with `error`, and `Retry-After` gives the seconds to wait. Show your default character until then.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a portrait can be drawn again.
